habitat: Pairs in summer near nest sites: road culverts, low causeways not over water, and aardvark holes in open savanna and grassland.
summary: A common summer resident. Large, with a blue cap extending below the eyes onto the ear coverts, and entirely orange-chestnut underparts. In flight the underwing coverts are buff, not white, and the tail-shafts are longer than a Mosque Swallow’s. The immature is duller above and paler on the cheeks, chin and throat, with shorter outer tail feathers. Adults give a soft warble and a strident trill. The flight is low and slow, with leisurely gliding. Months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Mosque Swallow has a white throat and upper breast, white underwing coverts and shorter tail-shafts. Red-breasted Swallow’s dark cap reaches below the eyes.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

calls.description: A soft warbling and a strident trill. Grade A song from Libreville, Gabon. The filename is French, Hirondelle-à-ventre-roux. No other grade A recording was in the set.
